title: Drupal Commerce Core unauthenticated access bypass exploited in the wild (SA-CONTRIB-2026-254, Highly critical 21/25); not in CISA KEV
why: Drupal's advisory SA-CONTRIB-2026-254 (Oct 28) states the flaw is actively exploited in the wild; covered by BleepingComputer, The Hacker News and SecurityWeek on Oct 30. Ostorlab and Rescana report it is not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.10.29, checked Oct 30). NVD has no score yet. Not a Microsoft product; no KEV entry. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Commerce Core to 3.3.13 (or 8.x-2.41) now, then audit recent orders for unpaid, re-priced or unexpectedly adjusted orders as Drupal advises.
product: Drupal Commerce Core 3.x before 3.3.13 and 8.x-2.x before 8.x-2.41

title: Oracle E-Business Suite unauthenticated SQLi-to-RCE (TCF servlet): exploit attempts seen in the wild days after the October CPU
why: Defused Cyber's EBS decoys recorded exploratory exploit attempts on Oct 27 (reported by BleepingComputer, The Hacker News and SecurityWeek). Public GitHub PoC/lab repos appeared on Oct 27, and Horizon3 has published the attack chain. It is not in CISA KEV: the KEV feed had no new entries this run. Oracle has not tagged it as exploited. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Apply the October 2026 CPU (MOS Note KA923) to every EBS 12.2.3-12.2.15 instance. Until then, remove /OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer from the EBS URL firewall allowlist, then hunt for unauthenticated POSTs to that path and for the oracle account spawning /bin/sh.
product: Oracle E-Business Suite 12.2.3 through 12.2.15 (Application Object Library, Core; /OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer)

title: Trojanized Claude Code VS Code extension 2.1.313 on Cursor marketplace / Open VSX planted persistent SSH backdoor (up to 5,000 users)
why: Cursor's security notice (Oct 29) confirms a malicious 2.1.313 build was served for ~11 hours to at most 5,000 users; analysis by OpenSourceMalware (OTX pulse), StepSecurity and Phorion, reported by BleepingComputer, THN and oss-security on Oct 30. Supply-chain compromise with no CVE, so no KEV entry; no Microsoft advisory or Defender guidance seen. Microsoft's own VS Code Marketplace was not reported to serve the bad build. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Find any endpoint that ran anthropic.claude-code 2.1.313, run Cursor's published check/remediation scripts, remove the unauthorized SSH key and persistence, and rotate credentials reachable from those hosts.
product: Anthropic.claude-code VS Code extension 2.1.313 installed from the Cursor extension marketplace / Open VSX on Oct 29, 2026 (2.1.312 and 2.1.314 clean)

title: WordPress Core unauthenticated RCE race during core upgrades (CVE-2026-119977): ~63,000 exploitation attempts in 24h; not in CISA KEV
why: Wordfence/Defiant telemetry shows active exploitation attempts (62,969 blocked in 24h per The Hacker News; SecurityWeek and GBHackers corroborate) polling wp-content/upgrade staging paths since the Oct 28 fix. No successful compromises confirmed yet. CVE published by Wordfence CNA Oct 30; not in CISA KEV (Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only). Not a Microsoft product.
action: Make sure every WordPress site is on 7.1.4 (or its branch's backport), and hunt logs for requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade plus new admin accounts, plugins or PHP files.
product: WordPress Core 4.7 through 7.1.3 (fixed in 7.1.4 and backported branch releases)

title: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chain: CISA adds CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527 to KEV; Ivanti ships fix for the privilege-escalation link
why: Not ahead: all three chained CVEs are now in CISA KEV (104935 on Oct 13; 111357 and 118527 on Oct 30).
action: Upgrade ICS to 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 or 22.8R2.6 now; because the actor runs in memory, do memory/network forensics rather than relying on the Integrity Checker.
product: Ivanti Connect Secure 22.8R2.5 and earlier, 25.1.1.2 and earlier (fixed 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1, 22.8R2.6); 22.7.x not affected

title: Citrix NetScaler pre-auth command injection (KEV): LevelBlue publishes new exploitation artifacts and hunt guidance
why: Not ahead: in CISA KEV since Sep 27, 2026.
action: Confirm NetScaler builds are at 14.1-73.46 / 13.1-64.29 or later and hunt authentication logs for the usernames LevelBlue describes; rebuild any appliance with indicators.
product: NetScaler ADC and Gateway before 14.1-73.37 / 13.1-64.23 (14.1-73.46 / 13.1-64.29 cover all Sep-Oct bulletins)

title: SonicWall SMA1000 pre-auth SSRF (CVSS 10.0): honeypot exploitation attempts since Oct 8, still not in CISA KEV
why: Previdian and Defused Cyber honeypots have recorded exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-102255 since Oct 8, reported by THN, SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer. It was not in CISA KEV as of catalog 2026.10.21 (Safeguard check), and the KEV additions on Oct 23 and Oct 26 did not include it. SonicWall's advisory still says there is no evidence of exploitation, and no successful compromise has been publicly confirmed. Rechecked Oct 28: the Oct 27 KEV additions (PolyShell, Brotli) do not include it. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade every SMA1000 to 12.4.3-03670 or 12.5.0-03082 or later, restrict Work Place exposure, and review appliance logs since Oct 6 for requests to internal services.
product: SonicWall SMA1000 6210/7210/8200v, 12.4.3-03526 and older, 12.5.0-02952 and older (includes the September fix builds)

title: Gotenberg unauthenticated RCE (ExifTool metadata-key injection, CVSS 9.8) exploited in the wild by multiple actors; not in CISA KEV
why: VulnCheck canaries recorded 1,358 exploitation events from 128 source IPs over 30 days, including an actor dropping a custom Go reverse shell (cache_base) in early October (VulnCheck blog, analysis Oct 24; THN ThreatsDay Oct 29); a separate cryptomining campaign is documented by The Hunter's Ledger. A public PoC and Nuclei template exist. VulnCheck notes it is NOT in CISA KEV (VulnCheck KEV since June). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade every Gotenberg container to 8.31.0 or later, keep port 3000 off untrusted networks behind an authenticating proxy, and hunt for POSTs to /forms/pdfengines/metadata/write and unexpected outbound connections from Gotenberg containers.
product: Gotenberg before 8.31.0 (/forms/pdfengines/metadata/write endpoint)

title: BeyondTrust Remote Support unauthenticated file upload to RCE (KEV): Rapid7 releases Metasploit module
why: Not ahead: in CISA KEV since Oct 16, 2026.
action: Verify BT26-05-RS is applied on every self-hosted Remote Support appliance (upgrade pre-24.3.1 first) and hunt for unknown PHP files, SUID shells and HAProxy changes.
product: Remote Support (self-hosted) 26.2.3 and earlier without BT26-05-RS patch; Privileged Remote Access shares code

title: eMudhra weak intermediate keys: Cloudflare sees ~22,000 forged-chain handshakes and a forged cert within an hour of disclosure
why: Not ahead: Microsoft blocked the intermediates through the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List on Oct 20; browsers and NSS also block them. Exposure now sits in non-browser trust stores.
action: Update runtimes, certifi/pip, container base images and app-bundled trust stores (incl. JetBrains Toolbox/IDEs), and test from inside containers that the eMudhra test chains fail.
product: Any TLS client or trust store still trusting the 8 eMudhra intermediates (emSign ECC Root CA - G3 / Sectigo cross-signs); JetBrains Toolbox before 3.9.1/3.8.2

title: EDK II PXE driver pre-boot RCE (CVSS4 9.5): Microsoft Project Mu ships fix, still no EDK II stable release or OEM firmware
why: TianoCore advisory GHSA-99cj-7hg9-mp4m, with Ars Technica, The Hacker News (Oct 28) and an oss-security thread (Oct 28). Microsoft's Project Mu fork has pulled the fix and tagged builds on Oct 26. Upstream EDK II still has no stable release with the fix, and the advisory reads 'Not patched currently'. No MSRC advisory, not in CISA KEV, no PoC or in-the-wild use reported. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Disable PXE/UEFI network stack where not needed, keep PXE on isolated provisioning VLANs, and track OEM firmware and distro edk2/OVMF updates for CVE-2026-97631.
vendor: TianoCore (EDK II); downstream AMI, Insyde, Phoenix, Project Mu, OVMF
product: EDK II NetworkPkg UefiPxeBcDxe up to edk2-stable202608 (fix merged Oct 15, PR 13302); vendor firmware updates pending

title: NUUO Crystal Server 3.19.0.85 unauthenticated upload.php web-root write to code execution: unpatched 0-day with claimed PoC
why: 0day Rubbish Research Team posted the unauthenticated upload-to-RCE on Full Disclosure Oct 28 with no vendor coordination and a claimed working PoC; no vendor advisory, no CVE, not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Keep NUUO Crystal management interfaces off the internet and restrict them to admin networks until NUUO ships a fix.
product: NUUO Crystal Server 3.19.0.85 (Crystal VM appliance)

title: Linux kernel IPv4 TCP handshake use-after-free (CVSS 9.8): Anthropic lab remote root on MPTCP listeners; Ubuntu/RHEL still unfixed, not in KEV
why: Anthropic demonstrated unauthenticated remote root on MPTCP listeners (exploit not published); BleepingComputer Oct 30 and Go security announcement. Ubuntu and RHEL still have no fixed kernel as of Oct 30; not in CISA KEV; no ITW reports. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Patch and reboot where fixed kernels exist; on Ubuntu/RHEL find MPTCP listeners (ss -M -tln; Go 1.24+ services), set GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0 or net.mptcp.enabled=0 where not needed, keep tcp_migrate_req=0, and consider dropping IPv4 packets with options at the edge.

title: Hugging Face trust_remote_code malware campaign returns: fake Qwen2 models drop GPU miners, reverse shells and SSH backdoors on inference servers
why: Pluto Security found 31 malicious repos across seven Hugging Face accounts; a second wave appeared within days of takedown and a near-identical model uploaded Oct 25 was still live when BleepingComputer checked (Oct 29). Flagship model reached 28,412 downloads. No CVE; no Microsoft advisory or KEV entry applies, and the article notes HF's scanners do not analyse bundled Python code. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Disable trust_remote_code by default, allowlist model sources, and check GPU inference hosts against Pluto Security's published indicators (via the BleepingComputer article); treat any host that loaded these models as compromised and rotate its credentials.
vendor: Hugging Face Hub (abused); targets Xinference, GPUStack
product: Self-hosted inference servers loading Hub models with trust_remote_code enabled

title: InternLM LMDeploy unauthenticated RCE via pickle in /update_weights (CVSS 9.3), reproduction code public
why: VulnCheck CVE published Oct 30; GitHub issue #4698 contains reproduction code showing request-controlled pickle deserialization. No fixed release is named in the sources and no ITW reports; not in CISA KEV. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Take LMDeploy api_server off untrusted networks (bind to localhost or front with auth and --api-keys) and block /update_weights until a fixed release is confirmed.
product: LMDeploy 0.9.0 through 0.18.0 (api_server)

title: FortiSandbox GUI unauthenticated auth bypass to command execution (CVSS 9.6, vendor E:F)
why: Fortinet FG-IR-26-185 and ZDI-26-771 describe the flaw, and Fortinet's vector carries E:F, but no public exploit has been found. Not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade FortiSandbox to 5.0.7 or 4.4.10 and restrict the management GUI to admin networks.

title: Tailworm: Tailscale 1.104.4 fixes SSH socket-forwarding root escalation and three more flaws (TS-2026-014 to 017), no CVEs
why: The researcher (Cyberdione Labs) published full details on Oct 25. Tailscale shipped 1.104.4 with bulletins TS-2026-014 to 017 on Oct 27. There are no CVE IDs, no in-the-wild reports, and it is not in KEV. The headscale findings remain unfixed. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade all Tailscale nodes to 1.104.4. Where you cannot, set TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1. On headscale, treat every SSH grant as root on the target.
product: Tailscale client before 1.104.4 (Tailscale SSH with forwarding, Serve); headscale up to 0.29.6 control-server findings not fixed by the client release

title: Supermicro BMC IPMI: unsigned, unencrypted commands accepted on live sessions (CVSS 9.8 CNA), plus 7 more BMC CVEs
why: Supermicro published advisories on Oct 26 and runZero (HD Moore) published research the same day. NVD published the CVEs on Oct 27. None of the nine CVEs was in CISA KEV at Rescana's check on Oct 27. No public PoC and no in-the-wild use reported. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Apply the BMC firmware Supermicro lists for each board, and keep IPMI (UDP 623) reachable only from an isolated management network.
product: Supermicro BMC firmware on select X12/X13 and other pre-X14 motherboards (X14 affected by CVE-2026-65213); fixed BMC firmware listed per board, two boards still TBD

title: WatchGuard Fireware OS: unauthenticated SIP-proxy RCE, FireCluster admin-action and Access Portal heap overflow among 18 Firebox fixes
why: WatchGuard published 18 Fireware OS advisories on Oct 27, seven of them CVSS 9.1 or higher, including an unauthenticated SIP-proxy stack overflow (CVE-2026-93857). WatchGuard says it knows of no exploitation and there is no public PoC (SecurityOnline, VulDB). None of the CVEs is in CISA KEV, even though earlier WatchGuard flaws are. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Fireboxes to Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 or 12.5.22. Until then, disable the SIP proxy and Access Portal where unused, isolate FireCluster links and restrict management interfaces.
product: Fireware OS before 2026.4 / 12.12.4 / 12.5.22 (Firebox appliances)

title: jackson-databind polymorphic-typing validator bypass via generic type arguments (CVSS 9.8), incomplete fix for CVE-2026-54512
why: The NVD record (Oct 28) and the GHSA advisory describe a working bypass: a gadget class wrapped in a generic type argument gets past the validator, with demonstrated Spring FileSystemXmlApplicationContext command execution. Not in CISA KEV and no in-the-wild reports. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade jackson-databind to 2.18.12, 2.21.8, 2.22.4, 3.1.8 or 3.2.4, and find any use of activateDefaultTyping or @JsonTypeInfo(use=CLASS) on untrusted input.

title: MLflow unauthenticated RCE via third-party scorer deserialization importing caller-placed artifact modules (CVSS 9.8)
why: The GitHub advisory GHSA-26p8-2jq9-3vq9 (Oct 27) describes RCE on unauthenticated MLflow servers. No PoC or in-the-wild use has been reported and it is not in CISA KEV. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade MLflow to 3.17.0 or later and put tracking servers behind authentication; never expose them to untrusted networks.
product: mlflow 3.12.0rc0 up to before 3.17.0

title: Brazilian Magecart group compromises Convertr's shared Plausible analytics script, skimming cards on all Convertr checkouts since Oct 24
why: Sansec research (OTX pulse, Oct 27) and BleepingComputer report an active supply-chain skimmer on every Convertr checkout since Oct 24. There is no CVE or vendor advisory. Not a Microsoft product and not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Convertr merchants should remove the third-party analytics script, enforce a CSP that blocks unknown script origins, and warn customers who checked out since Oct 24.
product: Convertr e-commerce platform checkouts (Brazil) loading the tampered analytics script

title: Dell PowerProtect Data Domain DSA-2026-416: unauthenticated root RCE, auth bypass and hard-coded key flaws (CVSS 9.8)
why: Dell advisory DSA-2026-416, with the CVEs published to NVD on Oct 28. Several flaws give an unauthenticated remote attacker root command execution or privileged account creation. No public exploit and no exploitation reported. Not in CISA KEV. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade DD OS to 8.9.0.0, 8.6.1.30, 8.3.1.50 or 7.13.1.90 or later, and restrict Data Domain/DDMC management interfaces to a dedicated management VLAN.

title: Juniper Session Smart Router/Conductor (JSA112183): two unauthenticated CVSS 9.8 flaws - admin takeover of un-onboarded routers and root command injection on Conductor
why: Juniper published bulletin JSA112183 on Oct 28 fixing 18 SSR flaws, including two unauthenticated 9.8s (NVD, SecurityOnline). They are not in CISA KEV. No public exploit or in-the-wild use has been reported yet. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade SSR and Conductor to 7.0.5/7.1.7/7.2.3, onboard staged routers to Mist/Conductor before exposing them, and restrict Conductor's management and salt ports to trusted networks.
product: Session Smart Router and Session Smart Conductor before 7.0.5, 7.1.7, 7.2.3

title: Sophos UTM (end-of-life) unauthenticated root RCE via email-proxy path traversal race; manual patch only
why: Sophos published a pre-auth RCE advisory and CVE on Oct 28 (CNA CVSS4 9.2), and its community blog urges urgent action for UTM Email Protection users. It is not in CISA KEV and no public exploit has been seen. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Install Sophos's manual UTM patch now or turn off email-proxy scanning, and plan to migrate off end-of-life UTM.
product: Sophos SG UTM, all versions (up to 9.724) with Email Protection proxy scanning enabled

title: Langflow OSS: IBM publishes 33 CVEs incl. unauthenticated RCEs (CVE-2026-110186, -104339) through 1.12.8; fixed only in 1.13.0
why: IBM bulletin 7294467 (Oct 28) and 33 CVE records (Oct 29) disclose unauthenticated code execution and auth bypass in every Langflow release through 1.12.8. HOL found no in-the-wild exploitation and none in CISA KEV as of Oct 29; a Metasploit module exists only for CVE-2026-93680 (tracked under the earlier Langflow ITW group, CVE-2026-0768). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Langflow to 1.13.0 (set LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD first; auto-login is disabled), keep Langflow behind an authenticating proxy, and rotate API keys stored in flows.
product: Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 (PyPI langflow, langflowai/langflow Docker); fixed in 1.13.0

title: Progress WS_FTP Server: unauthenticated admin-credential exposure (CVSS 10.0) plus 14 more flaws incl. 9.9 command injection
why: Progress released fixes Oct 29 for 15 WS_FTP Server flaws; CVE-2026-84295 lets an unauthenticated remote attacker obtain sensitive data including administrative credentials. No PoC or exploitation reported yet (SecurityOnline, OffSeq), and not in CISA KEV. Managed file transfer servers are a recurring mass-exploitation target. Runs on Windows but is not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade WS_FTP Server to 2025.0.4 or 2024.0.7 (covers all 15 CVEs), restrict the admin interface to management networks, and rotate WS_FTP administrator credentials after patching.

title: ClickHouse Server unauthenticated remote code execution 'under certain conditions' (CVSS 4.0 9.5), conditions undisclosed
why: ClickHouse (as CNA) published CVE-2026-116366 on Oct 30 (CVSS 4.0 9.5, AV:N/AC:H/PR:N) and a security-changelog PR lists patched releases. No public exploit verified (a Sploitus listing is unconfirmed), no in-the-wild reports, not in CISA KEV (TheHackerWire). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade ClickHouse Server to the latest patch release of a supported line and restrict network access to its HTTP/native ports to trusted clients until upgraded.
product: ClickHouse Server (affected/patched releases per ClickHouse security changelog; supported lines 26.3, 26.7, 26.8, 26.9)

title: 0day-rubbish batch: authenticated command injection in Moxa MAR-2000 (3), Raritan PX3 PDU and NETGEAR RAX120, unpatched
why: Five 0-day disclosures posted on Full Disclosure Oct 28 by 0day Rubbish with claimed PoCs and no vendor coordination; no advisories, CVEs or KEV entries. Rechecked Oct 30: CISA's Oct 29 KEV additions were only GitLab 97229 and Cisco 76418; still not in KEV. Rechecked Oct 31: CISA's Oct 30 KEV additions were Ivanti only, so still not in KEV.

product: Moxa MAR-2000 FWR_MAR2000_V1.0_Build_15010909; Raritan PX3 PDU G4 firmware 4.3.14; NETGEAR RAX120 V1.2.5.18

title: Canonical LXD/MicroCloud HTTPS listener trusts any cert in client chain: unauthenticated impersonation of trusted clients (CVSS 10)
why: Canonical security advisory and CVE published Oct 30 (referred from the Incus project); HN discussion. No PoC or exploitation reported (OffSeq: not known exploited); not in CISA KEV. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Upgrade LXD to 6.10.1 / 5.21.9 / 5.0.11 / 4.0.15 and keep the LXD API (8443) off untrusted networks.
product: LXD 4.0.14, 5.0.10, 5.21.8, 6.9 (fixed 4.0.15, 5.0.11, 5.21.9, 6.10.1); MicroCloud; snap-openstack clusterd
